The official OpenAI deprecations page (developers.openai.com) lists the following shutdown dates in the search results. Most of the detail comes from the page snippets, and the newest snapshot I found is from June 2026, so check the live page before relying on any of it.

- **December 11, 2026:** Older GPT-5 snapshots (gpt-5-2025-08-07, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-pro) and the o3-2025-04-16 and o3-pro-2025-06-10 snapshots. Recommended replacements are gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.5-pro. On June 11, 2026, OpenAI notified developers using older GPT-5 and o3 model snapshots of their removal from the API on December 11, 2026.
- **December 1, 2026:** gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, and chatgpt-image-latest, with gpt-image-2 as the suggested replacement. The notice of removal from the API on December 1, 2026 for older GPT Image models was sent June 2, 2026.
- **November 30, 2026:** The v1/prompts API and reusable prompt objects. They are scheduled to shut down on Nov 30, 2026.
- **August 10, 2026:** gpt-5.2-chat-latest and gpt-5.3-chat-latest, both pointing to gpt-5.5. These two chat-latest snapshots have an Aug 10, 2026 shutdown date.
- **January 6, 2027:** Fine-tuning job creation for active existing customers ends on this date. Inference on fine-tuned models is disabled only when the underlying base model is deprecated.

Secondary sources also mention an October 23, 2026 date for GPT-4-era models (gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo, o1, o4-mini), per a third-party guide that says it checked against the official page on July 31, 2026. A TrueFoundry post likewise lists October 23 for legacy GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4.1 Nano, GPT-4o, and o-series snapshots. I did not see this in the official page snippets, so verify it there. The same TrueFoundry post says OpenAI's published notice policy is at least six months for generally available models and at least three months for specialized variants such as Codex and chat-latest models.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

The official page is OpenAI's **Deprecations** page: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations. The older URL, platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations, should lead to the same content.

I couldn't open the page itself. My fetch attempts were refused, so everything below comes from search-result snippets and may be out of date. Check the live page before relying on any of it.

**Next models to be retired (today is 2026-10-16):**

| Shutdown date | What's retired | Suggested replacement |
|---|---|---|
| **Oct 23, 2026** (unconfirmed) | GPT-4-era models such as gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo, o1 and o4-mini | Not given in the snippets |
| **Nov 30, 2026** | The `v1/prompts` API and reusable prompt objects (not a model) | Not given in the snippets |
| **Dec 1, 2026** | gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, chatgpt-image-latest | gpt-image-2 |
| **Dec 11, 2026** | Older GPT-5 snapshots (gpt-5-2025-08-07, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-pro) and o3-2025-04-16 and o3-pro-2025-06-10 | gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.5-pro |
| **Jan 6, 2027** | Fine-tuning job creation for existing customers (not a model) | Not given in the snippets |

The Oct 23 date is the one to check first. I only saw it in third-party sources (a geeks.it.com guide and a TrueFoundry post), not in the official page's snippets. If it holds, it's the next retirement, only a week away.
